pages.text: Ashitey’s three-year-old cousin, Quaicoe, came to visit with his mother. Little Quaicoe felt hot and tired. His eyes were red and watery, his nose was running, and he coughed often. “He does not want to play today,” said Ashitey gently. “Mama, I think Quaicoe is sick.”
sentences: Ashitey’s three-year-old cousin, Quaicoe, came to visit with his mother.
Little Quaicoe felt hot and tired.
His eyes were red and watery, his nose was running, and he coughed often.
“He does not want to play today,” said Ashitey gently.
“Mama, I think Quaicoe is sick.”
pages.alt: Inside a calm Ghanaian family room, little three-year-old Quaicoe rests tiredly on his mother’s lap beside a colourful ball while ten-year-old Ashitey looks on kindly.

pages.text: Two days later, a red rash of tiny spots appeared on Quaicoe’s face and spread down his body. “We must take him straight to the clinic,” said his mother. Ashitey stayed safely at home with his own mother, keeping space from Quaicoe so the illness would not spread.
sentences: Two days later, a red rash of tiny spots appeared on Quaicoe’s face and spread down his body.
“We must take him straight to the clinic,” said his mother.
Ashitey stayed safely at home with his own mother, keeping space from Quaicoe so the illness would not spread.
pages.alt: Quaicoe’s mother gently carries little Quaicoe, who has tiny red spots on his cheeks, toward the courtyard gate while Ashitey waves kindly from the veranda.

pages.text: At the clinic, the nurse examined Quaicoe gently. “This illness is measles,” she explained. “It is caused by a tiny germ called a virus. Measles spreads through the air when a sick person coughs or sneezes, so it is very easy to catch, and it is never caused by anything a child did wrong.”

“It is caused by a tiny germ called a virus.
Measles spreads through the air when a sick person coughs or sneezes, so it is very easy to catch, and it is never caused by anything a child did wrong.”
pages.alt: In a clean, bright Ghanaian clinic room, a kind female nurse in a teal uniform gently examines little Quaicoe sitting on his mother’s lap.

pages.text: “Whenever someone near you has a high fever and a rash, tell a grown-up straight away so they can visit the clinic,” said the nurse. “A child with measles needs rest, plenty of clean fluids, and care at home away from others until the health worker says it is safe. Adults should also check everyone’s child health card.”
sentences: “Whenever someone near you has a high fever and a rash, tell a grown-up straight away so they can visit the clinic,” said the nurse.
“A child with measles needs rest, plenty of clean fluids, and care at home away from others until the health worker says it is safe.
Adults should also check everyone’s child health card.”
pages.alt: The kind nurse speaks reassuringly with Quaicoe’s mother across a tidy clinic desk beside a cup of water and a plain yellow child health booklet.

pages.text: “The best protection is the measles vaccine given at the clinic,” she added warmly. “It is free in Ghana’s child health programme and teaches the body to fight off the measles virus. Covering coughs with your elbow and washing hands with soap also help keep everyone well.”

pages.alt: The smiling nurse holds up a plain yellow child health booklet and a tiny vaccine vial beside a wordless wall picture of a healthy smiling toddler.

pages.text: Once Quaicoe recovered, Ashitey and his Primary 4 class drew a picture map about measles: its viral cause, its signs of fever, cough, runny nose, red eyes, and rash, and its prevention by vaccine and clean habits. That evening, Ashitey smiled as his mother showed him the vaccine ticks in his own health card.

activities.question: What causes measles?
options: A tiny germ called a virus

activities.question: What is the strongest way to protect a child from measles?
options: Getting the measles vaccine at the clinic

activities.prompt: Put the events of the story in order.
items: Quaicoe had a fever, cough, and red watery eyes.
A red rash of spots appeared, and his mother took him to the clinic.
The nurse explained that a virus causes measles and vaccines prevent it.
Ashitey’s class drew a picture map about measles.

glossary.definition: Many small red spots or patches appearing on the skin.
A contagious viral illness causing fever, cough, runny nose, red eyes, and a skin rash.
An extremely tiny germ that can cause illnesses such as measles or colds.
A protective medicine that prepares the body to fight off a specific disease.
